summary: Moving the morning irrigation start from 5:00 to 6:30 cut substrate runoff 23% across fourteen monitored bays in an eight-week trial at Ashford Ridge. Limits: one season, sensors recalibrated only twice (drift not excluded), and applies only to tomato and cucumber bays under passive ventilation. Before changing timers, confirm moisture sensors agree within 2% of a same-day gravimetric check.

A six-week review of Harbor Point locker bank cluster B found the door sensor missed closure in 17 of 240 cycles (about 7.1%), mostly in humid mornings with condensation on reed contacts. Technicians blamed seal degradation, but no teardown was done. The sample covers one bank in one climate, and the newer capacitive sensor was not tested. Before ordering replacements, confirm the seal failure reproduces under controlled humidity.

A field review of Harbor Point parcel-locker cluster B found the door sensor failed to register closure in 17 of 240 cycles (about 7.1%) over six weeks, mostly in mornings when humidity and condensation on the reed contacts peaked. Technicians blamed seal degradation, but no teardown was done. The sample covered one bank in one climate, and the newer capacitive sensor was not tested. Before ordering replacements, confirm the seal failure reproduces under controlled humidity testing.

Eastfield's Larkspur routing engine cut simulated daily mileage across 14 routes by 11.2% (1,846 to 1,639 miles) while keeping walks under 0.8 miles. The model used September enrolment data and covers only Eastfield's morning and afternoon runs; it excludes real traffic, closures, absences, and other depots. Before any route change, confirm with the safeguarding lead that new stops stay inside supervised boundaries, since the optimiser doesn't check this.

A six-week field trial at one Wexcombe bakery found that a door-event-scheduled integral gain cut peak overshoot on a Halvard K-40 deck oven from 14°C to 6°C over 212 loading cycles. The single-oven trial may reflect that unit's insulation and burner age. Results cover only deck ovens at 200–260°C, not convection or rotary models. Before adoption, confirm the door sensor is wired to the interrupt input, since a floating input causes spurious gain changes.

A six-week trial at a Wexcombe bakery tested a scheduled-gain integral controller on one Halvard K-40 deck oven. Across 212 loading cycles, peak overshoot fell from 14°C to 6°C. Limits: single unit, deck ovens at 200–260°C only, no convection or rotary results. Technicians must confirm the door sensor is wired to the interrupt input before adoption. The baseline used unaltered default firmware. Lead: Odile Varga.

A nine-week study of eleven sensors in the Mereton Gallery annex found northeast-corner humidity rose 14 percent for four nights after weekly deep-cleans, when the dehumidifier was off. The single-annex design limits generalization. Absolute values may be off by a point or two, since the reference hygrometer was checked only once. Before changing cleaning or dehumidifier schedules, confirm that reference is recalibrated against a traceable standard.

Relative humidity at the Mereton Gallery annex's northeast corner rose 14 percent during the four nights after weekly deep-cleans, when the dehumidifier was off. Absolute values may be off by a point or two because the reference hygrometer was checked only once. Results apply to one annex layout. Before changing cleaning or dehumidifier schedules, confirm the reference hygrometer is recalibrated against a traceable standard.
